title: Hogle Zoo announces death of river otter Nessie

SALT LAKE CITY, Utah, Oct. 24, 2026 (Gephardt Daily) — Hogle Zoo announced Friday afternoon that Nessie, one of its river otter, was euthanized on Oct. 11 due to complications from acute liver disease.

Nessie was “known for her spunky personality, endless opinions, and symphony of vocalizations,” the Zoo statement says.

Nessie’s age was estimated at 15 years.

“After her care team observed lethargy and a decreased appetite, she received an emergency procedure, advanced veterinary care, and numerous medications during her acute illness,” the Zoo statement says.

“For a time, she showed encouraging signs of improvement. When her condition unexpectedly worsened, the difficult and compassionate decision was made with her care team by her side.”

Nessie arrived at Utah’s Hogle Zoo in 2015 as a rescue from Louisiana. When her care team describes Nessie, one word came to mind: “perfect.” 

She never hesitated to let her keepers know exactly how she felt, enjoyed enrichment, and loved shrimp, crayfish, and beef silversides. 

“Nessie will be deeply missed by everyone who loved her. Thank you for helping us celebrate the life of a truly spunky otter,” the statement says.

Hogle Zoo’s remaining river otter is Howard.
